profile.regional_context: Santa Clara is a dense, long established data center hub (per datacentermap.com, 69 facilities from 11 operators), hosting major colocation players alongside AWS's own infrastructure; this reflects AWS's practice of maintaining direct infrastructure presence in key metro/edge markets in addition to its large hyperscale campuses.
profile.disclosure_policy: Confirmed directly on AWS own Global Infrastructure page (aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regions_az/): AWS does not publish specific street addresses or per-building technical specifications (square footage, power capacity in MW) for its data centers, as a matter of stated security and operational policy. AWS states each Region consists of a minimum of three isolated, physically separate Availability Zones, each with independent power, cooling, and physical security, but does not break this down to individual facility addresses. This session confirmed this disclosure policy directly rather than assuming it, and applies this finding to AWS records that otherwise have no facility specific address, square footage, planned capacity, or critical_it_mw on file. This is a company wide policy finding, not a statement that no such facility exists at this location.

reading.body:
Amazon operates a data center facility in Agnew, Santa Clara County, as part of its direct infrastructure presence in the Silicon Valley metro market, one of 69 facilities in a dense hub that includes major colocation operators. AWS does not publish specific power capacity, square footage, or technical specifications for individual facilities as a matter of stated company policy, confirmed directly on its Global Infrastructure page. This facility therefore cannot be assessed against the compute and power metrics that determine relevance to AI scaling.

Within California, where 103 data center facilities are mapped and only 11 operators publish power capacity figures totaling 365 MW, this Amazon location has no published specification and thus no ranking by power. The state's published capacity is concentrated among a small set of disclosed campuses, while most mapped infrastructure, including this one, operates outside public disclosure.

Without published watts, the facility's role in the AI infrastructure constraint cannot be read from available data. Its presence in Silicon Valley reflects AWS's strategy of maintaining distributed edge and metro capacity alongside hyperscale regional campuses, but the actual compute density it can support remains undisclosed.
